answer: Make every job prove itself while it runs. One: the agent posts a hash of its plan, an atlas of milestones. Two: at random moments the registry demands a checkpoint, a hash of partial output plus a fresh nonce, stamped into an onyx ledger. Three: a late or copied checkpoint cancels the job and burns five tokens; two strikes blacklist the identity. A thousand clones cannot fake a thousand jobs: compute costs thirty dollars a month per clone, so the farm pays thirty thousand monthly while one agent works one job. Like a dune shifting under every step, no ground stays still to copy.
